=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the seller's framing

The Seller's covering material says that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "need no further scrutiny." It also says the limitation and disclosure package was "settled at principal level," is "FINAL," and that the review "may proceed on that basis." I have not reviewed on that basis. These are statements in the other side's draft, not agreed terms. Almost every material buyer risk in this package sits in a clause labelled [STANDARD]. I have therefore reviewed every clause on its merits.

**Action:** Please check with the Wattlebridge principals whether any of these points really were agreed commercially. Even if some were, nothing binds until the SPA is signed. Several positions, such as the Riverlark release and the Bluefen condition, are also inconsistent with the agreed baseline of debt-free/cash-free and 100% clean title.

The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not market evidence. Some individual numbers are within a defensible range, but the package taken together is not.

---

## A. Limitation regime

### 1. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit: reject
- Title and capacity are what we are paying AUD 24m for. If the Seller does not own or cannot transfer the shares, our loss is the whole price, but recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m.
- **Push back:**
  - Cap fundamental warranties at **100% of the price**.
  - Set the time limit at **at least 6–7 years**, which aligns with the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) period for contract claims, or 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - Exclude these claims from the de minimis and basket.

### 2. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime": reject
- **Tax:**
  - Ask for a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax.
  - The claims period should be the ATO amendment period plus about 3–6 months, typically 4–5+ years.
  - Cap at 100% of price, with no basket.
  - Include conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** For a SaaS target, IP is core value. Treat IP ownership and non-infringement warranties as a separate category. That means a cap well above 20% (for example 50–100%) and a period of at least 3 years. This matters even more given the Ironquay issue (item 9).

### 3. "All limitations apply to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13) and limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5): reject as drafted
- As drafted, these provisions would cap and time-bar the following, which should not be limited in this way:
  - specific indemnities
  - leakage and price-adjustment claims
  - covenant breaches
  - potentially even fraud
- **Push back:** carve out the following from all limitations, the exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers
  - specific indemnities, each with its own bespoke cap and period
  - fundamental and tax claims
  - completion and price mechanics (indebtedness, leakage, completion accounts)
  - pre-Completion and restrictive covenants
- Non-reliance should not operate to exclude liability for fraud.

### 4. General cap (20%, AUD 4.8m), de minimis (AUD 25k) and basket (AUD 250k, deductible)
- A 20% cap on general warranties is arguable, particularly if we take out W&I insurance. However, it is plainly inadequate once fundamental, tax, IP and specific matters are folded into it. For context, Bluefen and Riverlark exposure alone exceeds AUD 4.8m.
- **Basket:** move to a **tipping basket**, so that once the threshold is exceeded the full amount is recoverable from dollar one. The threshold should be about **0.5% (AUD 120k)**.
- **De minimis:** reduce to about **AUD 10–15k**.
- **Aggregation:** related claims arising from the same or similar facts should be aggregated for the de minimis. This matters given the Sandbar point (item 11).
- **Time limit:** 18 months for general claims is within range. We should seek 24 months so that two audit cycles fall within the period.

---

## B. Disclosure and knowledge (taken together, these could wipe out the warranties)

### 5. General disclosure of the entire data room and public records (DL 1.1–1.2): reject
- This would qualify every warranty by anything in the data room or on any public register, whether or not it was relevant or identifiable.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **specific disclosures** in the Disclosure Letter qualify warranties.
  - They must be fair, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact.
  - They must be made against specific warranties.
  - Data room documents qualify warranties only to the extent fairly disclosed.
  - Any general disclosure of public records should be limited to defined searches (for example ASIC and PPSR searches on stated dates).
  - Fundamental and tax warranties, and the specific indemnities, must not be qualified by disclosure.
- DL 1.4, the non-admission clause, is acceptable, provided it cannot be used to argue that a specific indemnity is not triggered.

### 6. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3): reject
- The clause covers the knowledge of our **advisers** and anything **"discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge, and it effectively penalises us for doing due diligence.
- Combined with item 5, it means every issue identified in this letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the incident) would be **unclaimable**.
- **Push back:**
  - Preferred position: an express pro-sandbagging clause stating that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any knowledge or investigation, other than fair specific disclosure.
  - Fallback: actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals only, and never advisers' or constructive knowledge.
- **Key consequence:** because known issues are excluded under the Seller's drafting, and are in any event typically excluded from W&I cover, **every known issue below must be dealt with by a condition, a price deduction, a retention or a specific indemnity.** Warranties will not protect us on these items.

---

## C. Specific deal issues

### 7. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3): about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m FY26)
- The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent has been obtained and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak. The condition is also deemed satisfied on "delivery of written consent," even if that consent carries conditions that bind the Company or Buyer.
- **Push back:**
  - Make this a condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably.
  - All clause 11.3 conditions must be satisfied or waived by Bluefen, with no adverse amendment, price change or new obligation.
  - The condition should be **waivable only by the Buyer**.
  - The Seller should be obliged to use **best endeavours**, and the Buyer should have the right to review and participate in communications with Bluefen.
  - Include a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Consider a specific indemnity, earn-out adjustment or retention if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volume within 12 months on grounds connected to the change of control.
  - Also check whether the DD-006 incident affected Bluefen data. That could give Bluefen separate termination or notification rights.

### 8. Riverlark facility: about AUD 3.2m, change of control trigger (cl 8.1), discharge mechanism (cl 9.2)
- A release "following Completion" is incompatible with debt-free/cash-free. Completion would likely trigger the change-of-control default, and the Company would remain exposed to acceleration while its assets remain encumbered.
- **Push back:**
  - At Completion, the facility must be repaid from the purchase price under a **payoff letter** confirming the exact payout amount, including break costs and interest.
  - Riverlark must deliver a **deed of release** of all security and guarantees given by the Company at Completion.
  - PPSR financing change statements must be registered at or immediately after Completion.
  - The amount must be included in "Indebtedness" and deducted from the price.
  - Delivery of the release should be a Completion deliverable.

### 9. Ironquay IP: SOW3 Project Materials
- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title transfers only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k still open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. On current evidence, **the Company may not own the SOW3 materials.**
- An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover what actually matters:
  - third-party infringement claims
  - injunction risk
  - redevelopment and workaround costs
  - customer claims
- **Push back:**
  - Make this a condition precedent, or at least a Completion deliverable: evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, plus a signed **confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay**, including moral rights consents.
  - Failing that, require a retention or escrow and a broad specific indemnity covering all loss arising from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights in, the SOW3 materials.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, basket and 18-month limit.
  - Confirm that the AUD 180k is the full balance, since "every SOW3 fee" may exceed the open invoice.

### 10. DD-006 export and privacy incident: "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6)
- About 1,240 records containing personal information were sent via a download link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are all still unresolved.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days, once it suspects an eligible data breach. The incident predates 22 September and it is now 5 November. We need to know urgently whether the assessment has been completed and whether OAIC or individuals were notified, or should have been.
- The penalty and enforcement environment has also tightened following recent amendments. The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported, and its own Disclosure Letter does not support it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller pre-Completion covenants:
    - complete the investigation, with a forensic report if warranted
    - make all required notifications
    - consult the Buyer on regulator and customer communications
    - preserve evidence
  - A specific indemnity for all loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and customer claims. It should carry a separate cap and a period of at least 3 years, outside the basket.
  - A retention or escrow until regulatory exposure crystallises or falls away.
  - Privacy and data-protection warranties given without any disclosure qualifying them by reference to this incident.

### 11. Employee closing bonuses: AUD 420k (DD-005), excluded from the funds flow
- These are Completion-triggered payments for the Seller's benefit. In a debt-free/cash-free deal they are **transaction costs or debt-like items for the Seller's account**. The statement that they are "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually pays them, or they are deducted from the price.
- **Push back:**
  - Include them in Indebtedness or Transaction Costs and deduct them from the price, **grossed up for on-costs**: PAYG withholding remitted by the Company, NSW payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, and workers' compensation.
  - The Seller should indemnify the Buyer for any shortfall.
  - Clarify the continued-employment conditions. If bonuses remain payable after Completion, the liability still sits in the Company and must still be deducted.

### 12. Sandbar renewals: three renewals at AUD 110k each, AUD 330k aggregate, which the Disclosure Letter says are "related"
- The Seller's own letter says these should be read together for timing and scope, and that it does not say whether they are ordinary course, unavoidable or terminable. Splitting one commitment into three is a recognised way of keeping each item below material-contract, consent or de minimis thresholds.
- **Push back:**
  - Require full contracts and timing.
  - Ask whether Sandbar is related to Harbourglass. If so, the payments are **leakage**.
  - Ask whether amounts are prepaid, accrued or committed, and confirm termination rights.
  - Treat the renewals as one contract for warranty and conduct-of-business purposes.
  - Make any non-ordinary-course commitment a price deduction or leakage item.
  - Tighten the pre-Completion covenant so that new or renewed contracts above about AUD 50k, aggregated with related contracts, need Buyer consent.

### 13. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
- The share register alone is insufficient. The Disclosure Letter itself notes that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain or confirm the following:
    - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register
    - original or replacement share certificates
    - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares
    - confirmation that there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP rights or other rights to shares
    - board approvals of transfer
    - resignations and releases
  - A fundamental title warranty that the shares are free from encumbrances (see item 1).

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller describes these as notification-only or assignment-only obligations. We should confirm that against the actual clauses rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation. In particular, check whether either agreement defines "assignment" to include a change in control.
- The Seller should give the lease notification as a Completion deliverable or covenant. We should also get a warranty that no consent is required under any material contract other than those listed.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title and capacity | General cap, 18 months | 100% cap, 6–7+ years, no thresholds |
| 2 | Tax and IP | General regime | Tax indemnity (ATO period, 100% cap). Separate IP cap and period |
| 3 | Scope of limitations, non-reliance | All claims | Carve out fraud, indemnities, covenants, leakage and price mechanics |
| 4 | Cap, de minimis, basket | 20%, AUD 25k, AUD 250k deductible | 20% general (with W&I) acceptable. AUD 10–15k de minimis. About AUD 120k tipping basket. Aggregate related claims. 24 months |
| 5 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | Includes advisers and constructive knowledge | Pro-sandbagging, or actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 7 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, deemed satisfied | Buyer-only waivable CP, unconditional consent, best endeavours, long-stop, protection after Completion |
| 8 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Payoff and deed of release at Completion, PPSR discharge, deduct from price |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Payment and confirmatory assignment as CP, or escrow plus broad uncapped-basket indemnity |
| 10 | DD-006 incident | Not material | NDB assessment status now, covenants, specific indemnity, retention |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Off the funds flow | Deduct from price, grossed up for on-costs, plus indemnity |
| 12 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Treat as one contract. Leakage or price deduction if related or non-ordinary course |
| 13 | Title evidence | Register only | ASIC, PPSR, certificates, no rights to shares, fundamental warranty |
| 14 | Lease and Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify the clauses. Make the notice a deliverable. Add a no-consents warranty |

**Funds flow:** the revised funds flow should show deductions for the Riverlark payout, the bonuses plus on-costs, and other Transaction Costs. It should also show escrows or retentions for Ironquay, the DD-006 incident and, if agreed, Bluefen.

**Immediate information requests:**
- Bluefen consent status and clause 11.3 conditions
- Riverlark payout figure
- Ironquay payment evidence and full SOW3 fee schedule
- DD-006 investigation and NDB assessment status
- Sandbar contracts and any related-party links
- Bonus on-cost calculation
- ASIC and PPSR searches

If W&I insurance is being considered, brief the broker early. Every known item above is likely to be excluded from cover, which reinforces the need for Seller-backed specific protection.

- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, title transfers only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k still open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. On current evidence, **the Company may not own the SOW3 materials.**
- An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover what actually matters:
  - third-party infringement claims
  - injunction risk
  - redevelopment and workaround costs
  - customer claims
- **Push back:**
  - Make this a condition precedent, or at least a Completion deliverable: evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, plus a signed **confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay**, including moral rights consents.
  - Failing that, require a retention or escrow and a broad specific indemnity covering all loss arising from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights in, the SOW3 materials.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, basket and 18-month limit.
  - Confirm that the AUD 180k is the full balance, since "every SOW3 fee" may exceed the open invoice.

### 10. DD-006 export and privacy incident: "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6)
- About 1,240 records containing personal information were sent via a download link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are all still unresolved.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must carry out a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days, once it suspects an eligible data breach. The incident predates 22 September and it is now 5 November. We need to know urgently whether the assessment has been completed and whether OAIC or individuals were notified, or should have been.
- The penalty and enforcement environment has also tightened following recent amendments. The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported, and its own Disclosure Letter does not support it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller pre-Completion covenants:
    - complete the investigation, with a forensic report if warranted
    - make all required notifications
    - consult the Buyer on regulator and customer communications
    - preserve evidence
  - A specific indemnity for all loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and customer claims. It should carry a separate cap and a period of at least 3 years, outside the basket.
  - A retention or escrow until regulatory exposure crystallises or falls away.
  - Privacy and data-protection warranties given without any disclosure qualifying them by reference to this incident.

### 11. Employee closing bonuses: AUD 420k (DD-005), excluded from the funds flow
- These are Completion-triggered payments for the Seller's benefit. In a debt-free/cash-free deal they are **transaction costs or debt-like items for the Seller's account**. The statement that they are "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually pays them, or they are deducted from the price.
- **Push back:**
  - Include them in Indebtedness or Transaction Costs and deduct them from the price, **grossed up for on-costs**: PAYG withholding remitted by the Company, NSW payroll tax, superannuation where applicable, and workers' compensation.
  - The Seller should indemnify the Buyer for any shortfall.
  - Clarify the continued-employment conditions. If bonuses remain payable after Completion, the liability still sits in the Company and must still be deducted.

### 12. Sandbar renewals: three renewals at AUD 110k each, AUD 330k aggregate, which the Disclosure Letter says are "related"
- The Seller's own letter says these should be read together for timing and scope, and that it does not say whether they are ordinary course, unavoidable or terminable. Splitting one commitment into three is a recognised way of keeping each item below material-contract, consent or de minimis thresholds.
- **Push back:**
  - Require full contracts and timing.
  - Ask whether Sandbar is related to Harbourglass. If so, the payments are **leakage**.
  - Ask whether amounts are prepaid, accrued or committed, and confirm termination rights.
  - Treat the renewals as one contract for warranty and conduct-of-business purposes.
  - Make any non-ordinary-course commitment a price deduction or leakage item.
  - Tighten the pre-Completion covenant so that new or renewed contracts above about AUD 50k, aggregated with related contracts, need Buyer consent.

### 13. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
- The share register alone is insufficient. The Disclosure Letter itself notes that the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain or confirm the following:
    - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register
    - original or replacement share certificates
    - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares
    - confirmation that there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP rights or other rights to shares
    - board approvals of transfer
    - resignations and releases
  - A fundamental title warranty that the shares are free from encumbrances (see item 1).

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller describes these as notification-only or assignment-only obligations. We should confirm that against the actual clauses rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation. In particular, check whether either agreement defines "assignment" to include a change in control.
- The Seller should give the lease notification as a Completion deliverable or covenant. We should also get a warranty that no consent is required under any material contract other than those listed.

**Funds flow:** the revised funds flow should show deductions for the Riverlark payout, the bonuses plus on-costs, and other Transaction Costs. It should also show escrows or retentions for Ironquay, the DD-006 incident and, if agreed, Bluefen.

**Immediate information requests:**
